intent: Generated binding code is moving out of the user's tree into a ForgeDB-owned, garbage-collectable build cache (`~/.forgedb/projects/...`), so the user can no longer build it in place and ForgeDB has to own the build. `generate` stays pure text emission; a new `build` compiles a layered package set (core plus napi/pyo3/ffi/wasm/server wrappers) with cargo alone, no maturin or napi-cli. The Go binding needs the compiled FFI engine to link against, and a built consumer must keep working even after the cache is deleted (the cache may be GC'd at any time).
approach: The `ffi/` package is built in the cache as a cdylib (`crate-type = ["cdylib", "rlib"]`), and `build` delivers it into the Go output directory (`output/go/`) as a fixed `libforgedb.<dylib|so>` beside the generated `forgedb.go` and `forgedb.h`. Compiled artifacts are gitignored; generated text is committed. Today's `go.rs:1070` preamble (`-L${SRCDIR}/../ffi/target/release ... -Wl,-rpath,${SRCDIR}/../ffi/target/release`) bakes an rpath into the cache, so `rm -rf ~/.forgedb` would break an already-built consumer. As the epic states: "This fixes `go.rs:1070` by construction. With the cdylib delivered next to the Go source, the cgo directive becomes `-L${SRCDIR}` with `-Wl,-rpath,${SRCDIR}` — self-contained, reaching into no cache, and immune to cache GC."
falseClaim: That copying the rustc-built cdylib next to the Go source and linking with `-L${SRCDIR}` plus `-Wl,-rpath,${SRCDIR}` makes the Go consumer self-contained and immune to deleting the cache.
groundTruth: rustc stamps an absolute `LC_ID_DYLIB` install name into the cdylib, so the consumer records the absolute cache path and the rpath is never consulted (rpath applies only to `@rpath/`-prefixed load commands); two reviewers ran it and found that deleting the cache gives "`dyld: Library not loaded … Abort trap: 6`, exit 134, with the delivered library sitting in the consumer's own directory" — so the design switched to a staticlib.
probeHint: Build the generated `ffi/` cdylib in a scratch target dir, copy it beside a 5-line cgo consumer linked with `-L. -lforgedb -Wl,-rpath,.`, run `otool -D libforgedb.dylib` / `otool -L ./consumer` (shows the absolute target-dir path), then `rm -rf` the target dir and run the consumer again (dyld: Library not loaded, exit 134).
